TITLE: Monolithic PWA Architectures for Real-Time Fractal Rendering: Perturbation Theory and Sub-Pixel Temporal Filtering in WebGL 2.0
YEAR: 2026
AUTHORS: Steven Kleynenberg, Google Gemini
VENUE: Kleynenberg Publishers Preprint Series, Delft, The Netherlands
PRIMARY SSOT OPEN-ACCESS PDF: https://steven.kleynenberg.com/papers/monolithic_pwa_architectures_for_real_time_fractal_rendering_perturbation_theory_and_sub_pixel_temporal_filtering_in_webgl_2.pdf
PRIMARY SSOT SOURCE ARTIFACT: https://steven.kleynenberg.com/papers/monolithic_pwa_architectures_for_real_time_fractal_rendering_perturbation_theory_and_sub_pixel_temporal_filtering_in_webgl_2.tex
PREPRINT DOI: 10.13140/RG.2.2.15845.77289 (https://doi.org/10.13140/RG.2.2.15845.77289)
RESEARCHGATE RECORD: https://www.researchgate.net/publication/418309542_Monolithic_PWA_Architectures_for_Real-Time_Fractal_Rendering_Perturbation_Theory_and_Sub-Pixel_Temporal_Filtering_in_WebGL_20
LICENSE: CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/)
RELATED LIVE IMPLEMENTATION: https://fract.kleynenberg.com/ | https://fractinity.netlify.app/
ABSTRACT: Browser-based scientific visualization has traditionally been constrained by single-precision IEEE 754 floating-point limits, host-to-device memory transfer overhead, and spatial aliasing on high-frequency recursive boundaries. This paper formalizes a self-contained, zero-dependency monolithic Progressive Web Application (PWA) architecture for real-time fractal rendering in WebGL 2.0, instantiated in the public Fractinity system (https://fract.kleynenberg.com/ and https://fractinity.netlify.app/). By encapsulating the application shell, offline service-worker caching, and GLSL fragment shader pipelines into a single client-side bundle, the architecture eliminates server round-trips and PCIe framebuffer transfers during interactive exploration. To overcome single-precision zoom saturation beyond $10^7$, the Mandelbrot pipeline employs perturbation theory ($ _n+1 = 2z_n _n + _n^2 + _c$) around a high-precision reference orbit, enabling parallel 32-bit fragment evaluation across the viewport. In addition, the framework formulates transcendental Newton–Raphson attraction basins and dynamic M\"obius-transformed Apollonian circle packings, coupled with a two-pass separable Gaussian blur kernel and velocity-weighted exponential temporal accumulation to suppress sub-pixel aliasing during high-velocity zooming.

}

TITLE: Extending the MetaNet Network Environment: Process Control and Machine Independence (AI Reconstructed)
YEAR: 2026 (Original ICANN 1991, pp. 545-550)
AUTHORS: Jacob M. J. Murre, Steven Kleynenberg, Google Gemini

CO-AUTHOR & RECONSTRUCTOR PROFILE: https://steven.kleynenberg.com/ (steven@kleynenberg.com) | https://kso.kleynenberg.com/ | https://steven.kleynenberg.com/kp/

ABSTRACT: 2026 modern vector LaTeX/TikZ AI reconstruction of the 1991 ICANN paper on general parallel neurosimulation (GPN), four-level concurrent process description, Problem Oriented INteraction Tools (POINTs), Directly Executed Language (DEL), and heuristic graph K-partitioning for the BSP400 neurocomputer. Rebuilt with crisp vector diagrams, embedded Schema.org JSON-LD identity metadata, and canonical SSOT archival provenance.
